primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander
primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators III: Pseudo-Differential Operators
primary_antecedent.edition: Springer 2007, reprint of the corrected 1994 edition
primary_antecedent.locator: Propositions 24.7.1 and 24.7.1-prime, printed pages 465–467; actual Banach and boundary-value hypotheses and the graph-topology argument.
primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Independent detailed domain bridge: one Banach-controlled distribution order, coefficient-uniform normal recovery with one negative tangential source norm, complete actual graph topology and trace convergence for changing coefficients.

source_correspondence: B0 states the actual full negative tangential source norm and compact smooth matrix family. It proves the local graph estimate without a real-principal or positivity assumption. The conversion from admissible cone-restricted source tests is explicitly not asserted.

B1 proves completeness of flat compact tests and constructs an interior approximation with every derivative controlled by Taylor flatness. This identifies their distribution pairing independently of any ambient extension.

B2 applies Baire to the entire Banach unit ball to obtain one finite distribution order. The Fourier Sobolev bound, complex Hahn–Banach and Hilbert duality give an actual uniform negative Sobolev extension. No linear choice of extensions is assumed.

B3 fixes all nested base cutoffs before the iteration. Every mapping constant depends on finitely many complete coefficient derivatives, uniformly bounded on the compact parameter family. Inversion of a highest normal matrix is on the left and retains all ordered derivatives.

B4 retains every term of the differential cutoff equation. The source weight q^(r-1) lambda^(t-1) is bounded by lambda^(-N-2) through the last step. The pure normal recovery theorem uses actual restriction quotient norms, not an arbitrary differentiated extension.
B5 performs exactly N+2 steps, preserving r+t=-N and ending in Hbar^(2,-N-2). Its three exact weight inequalities give the actual solution, first normal derivative and second normal derivative norms.

B6 proves the negative-order trace bounds using actual absolutely continuous representatives. Cutoff trace identities retain the normal derivative of the cutoff; the result agrees with intrinsic traces when the intrinsic representative is available.

B7 proves completeness of the actual source graph using the Banach and L2 limits and their interior distributional identity. It identifies the prescribed value map on the smooth graph closure. Banach density is not silently replaced by graph density.

B8 proves strong graph convergence while the coefficients change. Uniform recovery on a larger collar controls the full coefficient difference in the same source norm; a second fixed-operator estimate on differences proves convergence of both actual traces. No parameter derivative of the solution family is used.

B9 records the remaining cone-tester conversion, other uniform regimes and finite observation argument. Full normal-source smoothness is not imposed as an additional gate for an L2 observation estimate.

Three complete solutions compute the N=2 index sequence, an exact sourced boundary layer with bounded second but unbounded third normal derivative, and an H1 zero-Dirichlet sequence whose normal trace fails to converge because its source norm diverges.
The original figure uses exact Sobolev-index lattice points and exact affine logarithmic derivative norms.

Twenty-six exact checks, 223 parsed formulas, 29 numbered displays and thirteen inspected lesson captures support this review. They do not replace the Baire, quotient-space or graph-completeness proofs.
